title: Add the add-only statusLine settings writer to hooks_wiring
action:
SLICE 1, part 1 of 4. Add three public items to src/onboard/hooks_wiring.rs, in the existing '── statusline opt-in ──' section. Touch NO other file — plan.rs, apply.rs and mod.rs are other cells.

1. `pub const STATUSLINE_COMMAND: &str` — the exact command string onboarding writes:

    [ -f "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}/.claude/statusline-command.sh" ] && bash "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}/.claude/statusline-command.sh"

   The `[ -f … ] &&` guard is load-bearing, not decoration: .claude/settings.json is a TRACKED, team-shared file and the vendored .sh is not in GITIGNORE_BLOCK_PATTERNS, so a teammate's fresh clone or a linked worktree has the pointer without the file and would get a shell error on every prompt.

2. `pub fn statusline_settings_absent(repo_root: &Path) -> bool` — true ONLY when <repo>/.claude/settings.json is missing, or its text is empty/whitespace, or it parses as a JSON OBJECT carrying no `statusLine` key. It MUST answer FALSE when the file exists but does not parse, or parses to something that is not an object at the top level. Do NOT reuse `read_json_if_exists` (util.rs:55-61) — it collapses broken and missing into the same None, and a naive 'no key -> write' would rewrite a host's settings file as bare {"statusLine": …}, the exact bug merge_hooks_file was hardened against (see this file's own l.197-229 and the tests at l.752-789). Read the raw text and parse it yourself. A present `statusLine` of ANY shape — object, string, null, false — counts as declared and answers false: a present value is the user's preference.

3. `pub fn merge_statusline_settings(settings_path: &Path) -> Merged` — returns the whole-file text with the canonical entry added, plus `changed`. It preserves EVERY foreign top-level key and their order (mirror how merge_hooks_file builds `out` at l.261-262 and serialises with jsjson::stringify_pretty + a trailing newline). Add-only: if `statusLine` is already present, return the file unchanged with changed=false. On a file that does not parse or is not an object, return unchanged with changed=false — this writer has NO failure mode and must never produce an Err, because a refusal would turn a default into a blocker for every host with a broken settings file. On a missing/empty file, produce a fresh object holding just `statusLine`.

TESTS, in this file's existing `mod tests`, beside statusline_opt_in_only_for_project_level_references (l.1023):
  - THE ROUND TRIP, the most important case: statusline_opt_in() returns TRUE for a settings file whose statusLine.command is STATUSLINE_COMMAND. Get this wrong and every host silently un-adopts on the next run — no re-vendoring, managed.statusline dropped, and nothing says so. The oracle at l.1039-1049 already shows that `bash "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"/.claude/statusline-command.sh` does NOT match while the `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}` form does; pin it rather than trusting the reading.
  - absent file, empty file, object-without-the-key -> absent == true
  - unparseable text, top-level array, top-level string -> absent == false
  - statusLine present as an object / a string / null / false -> absent == false
  - merge on a file carrying "model" and "hooks" -> those keys and their values survive byte-for-byte, exactly one key is added
  - merge is idempotent: merging twice changes nothing the second time (changed == false)
  - merge on a broken file returns changed == false and text equal to the input

RED FIRST: write the round-trip case first and watch it fail to compile / fail for the documented reason before the const exists.

truths: statusline_opt_in() is proven TRUE against STATUSLINE_COMMAND by a test.
A settings file that does not parse is never rewritten and never blocks: absent==false, merge returns changed==false.
Foreign top-level keys and their order survive the merge byte-for-byte.
